adr_goal_revalidation.scope: offline decoder investigation; no native capture, workload, build, or production edit

must: capture parent PID, TID, /proc comm/exe, starttime, and the complete /proc/<pid>/task TID set before and after the handoff
set every observed recorder TID to exactly [30], preferably with an all-tasks operation or per-TID calls, then read back each TID mask
reject if parent is not the bound /usr/bin/perf, if any set/readback fails, if any TID remains outside [30], or if the TID set changes unexpectedly
bind the exact perf SHA and forbid --threads, --aio, --affinity, -C, BPF sideband, and other options that add/move streaming threads unless separately bound and checked
minimum_admission_obligations.reason: sched_setaffinity and sched_getaffinity are per-thread; process-level PID syntax addresses the main thread

must: record monotonic sequence and timestamps for launcher start, parent identity, parent TIDs-before, affinity set/readback, parent TIDs-after, launcher readback, and native exec
perform the parent handoff before native exec and abort before native exec on EPERM, ESRCH, identity mismatch, or incomplete readback
retain same target PID/TID across launcher and native exec; bind native executable/build ID and cwd/env

do not use an inner taskset launched while recorder is CPU30 unless startup samples are explicitly excluded and independently validated; that ordering can create CPU30 samples before taskset applies CPU31
minimum_admission_obligations.reason: enable_on_exec starts measurement at the launcher Python exec; the clean proposed ordering keeps launcher/native target on CPU31 throughout

must: retain --per-thread with inherit disabled and no -C; verify header fields and CPU_MAP/dummy per-thread scope
require every decoded target sample PID/TID to equal native exec PID/TID and every sample CPU to equal 31
separate launcher/pre-native records from native marker records; do not infer recorder CPU from sample CPU
reject any target sample CPU30, unexpected fork/clone/descendant exit, or DSO/build-ID drift
minimum_admission_obligations.reason: sample CPU identifies target execution, while recorder placement is proven by live/sideband affinity records

must: retain raw PERF_RECORD_LOST sum == 0 and terminal PERF_RECORD_LOST_SAMPLES == 0 as separate gates; never add the two domains
retain raw STACK_USER bounds and marker-count/share gates unchanged
serial execution, fresh exclusive output roots, stop on first child failure, no retry or selective replacement
bind all helper/plan/runner/launcher/perf/taskset/python/source/binary hashes before GO and recheck source/binary custody
minimum_admission_obligations.reason: CPU separation tests placement only and cannot relax the failed 0975 loss or ancestry gates

must: before any native cohort, execute one authorized harmless exact-wrapper control through the real perf/Python launch boundary
make the control write parent PID/TID/starttime and before/after masks from the launcher, verify native exec identity, and retain raw perf/header/terminal evidence
exercise actual Popen/exec and all-TID affinity code rather than only mocks; a control with no samples cannot establish a sample-CPU claim, so sample CPU remains a gate in native children
minimum_admission_obligations.reason: the proposed cross-process affinity handoff is the new behavior and needs real boundary evidence

non_claims: No native workload, build, or harmless control was run for this review.
No claim is made that CPU30 is idle, that all PMU overflow/interrupt work moved to CPU30, or that the split will eliminate loss.
No period, buffer, marker, ancestry, or no-retry gate is relaxed.
No CPU split design is admitted until a frozen plan/helper set and the exact boundary control satisfy the obligations above.

limits: moving only getppid() changes the perf thread-group leader/main thread; it does not move other perf TIDs
a recorder-side helper could remain on CPU31 unless the exact perf topology proves it cannot exist or every recorder TID is moved and verified
a loss-free split is a diagnostic comparison, not proof that CPU31 contention caused the earlier loss
ordering: outer taskset starts perf and target launcher with inherited CPU31
launcher verifies its own affinity is exactly [31]
launcher identifies parent as the actual perf process and moves the parent recorder thread set to CPU30
launcher verifies its own affinity remains [31] and recorder thread set is [30]
launcher execs the native target without changing the target PID/TID
why_no_native_sample_cpu30_is_plausible: perf_event_attr.enable_on_exec enables the target event after execve; with the launcher Python exec started under CPU31, startup and native execution begin with target affinity [31]
sched_setaffinity changes the identified parent/main thread, while execve preserves the calling target thread affinity
PERF_SAMPLE_CPU reports the CPU where the target sample was taken, not the CPU on which perf drains its mmap

retained_evidence.role: prior bounded placement analysis; not a capture admission
prior serial run stopped on child 02 raw loss; no retry/all-12 conclusion
prior corrected audit; child-02 retained task records pass but lifetime task history not proven after raw loss

key_points: --per-thread uses per-thread mmaps and disables inheritance; -C is ignored with --per-thread
--affinity controls the trace reading thread policy and is not a dedicated spare-CPU placement guarantee
--threads is a parallel streaming mode and is mutually exclusive with per-thread
sched_setaffinity is per-thread; fork inherits affinity and execve preserves it
enable_on_exec enables the event after execve and PERF_SAMPLE_CPU records the executing CPU
source_interpretation.local_installed_docs: perf 7.0.14 man perf-record and man perf_event_open were inspected; upstream source link is a semantic cross-check, not an exact binary provenance claim
